subject: Request: expedited SLA uplift for AtlasAI pilot
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: expedited SLA uplift for AtlasAI pilot

Team —

Quick heads-up: AtlasAI (contact: Ben Moore) asked if we can commit to a higher availability and tighter p95 for their 90-day pilot. They want an "enterprise-like" P95 of 120ms for text generation on the primary route for the duration of the pilot and a 99.9% uptime target. This is for a paid pilot (ATL-2027-042) that could convert to a Dedicated Reserved deal if their performance benchmarks are met.

Attached is their formal request and the mutual action plan. High-level asks from AtlasAI:
- P95 target: 120ms for their primary inference route (expected 800–1,200 RPS bursts during business hours)
- 99.9% availability for the pilot window
- Response plan and credit schedule for outages >30m

Asking for quick cross-functional guidance:
1) Product: feasibility + what configuration we'd need (dedicated pool? burst capacity?) and rough lead time to provision.
2) Infra/SE (Karthik): viability of hitting p95 at that QPS with their model (they'll use a 13B family variant) and what trade-offs (quantization/replicas) look like.
3) Legal/Revenue (Laura): any contract redlines we should require for a short pilot and suggested guardrails.

We need to reply to Ben with a proposed approach by EOD so they can lock dates.

Attachments: atlasai_sla_request_v1.pdf, atlasai_mutual_action_plan.xlsx

Thanks —
Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: expedited SLA uplift for AtlasAI pilot

Jasmine —

Thanks for the ping. A few quick technical clarifications before we commit:
- Do they expect the P95 at 1) tail latency observed at our edge (i.e., application-level) or 2) just inference engine time? We need to know whether networking and client-side timeouts are in-scope.
- What sequence length and prompt distribution should we plan for? Short prompts (<=128 tokens) vs long (>=512) change kernel selection significantly.
- Do they require model pinning (exact model hash) for the pilot? That impacts cache warmup and p95 during bursts.

Prelim thought: to attain 120ms p95 at 1k RPS with a 13B model, we likely need a small dedicated pool with continuous batching optimized for their request distribution and prefix caching enabled. If they insist on model pinning + high variability in prompt length, the safe path is a dedicated pool with 2x baseline replicas and a warmup window.

I can produce a short runbook and capacity estimate by EOD if you want — need the sequence-length distribution and an example traffic day.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 13:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: expedited SLA uplift for AtlasAI pilot

Thanks — adding product context.

Options we can propose to AtlasAI (ordered by operational risk):
1) Short pilot on Dedicated-Preview: spin a small dedicated pool (pinned model variant) for the 90-day window. Pros: predictable performance, easier to guarantee p95. Cons: longer lead time and higher unit cost.
2) Hosted + elevated routing: keep them on hosted but route their traffic to a guarded capacity tier with prefix caching and strict batching config. Pros: faster to start, lower cost. Cons: harder SLA enforcement during noisy neighbors.
3) Hybrid: initial 30 days Hosted with burst fallback to Dedicated during peak windows; reassess and flip to Dedicated if conversion looks likely.

For a commitment letter to the customer we need:
- Clear ramp plan with measurable observability (per-route p95 dashboards in Console)
- Escalation matrix and on-call contact (we should include SRE on rotation)
- Trial termination clause and credit formula for downtime >30m

Karthik — please include the capacity estimate. Laura — we will need minimal contractual language for a pilot; can we scope out a short amendment or an MSA addendum?

Aisha
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: expedited SLA uplift for AtlasAI pilot

Team —

From a legal/revenue perspective I recommend we standardize on a 90-day pilot addendum with the following guardrails:
- Explicit pilot scope (routes, model hash(es), region).
- Limited service credit capped at X% of pilot fees (we can negotiate X — recommend 10% cap for pilot).
- Termination notice: 7 days for material SLA breach.
- Data residency confirmation (AtlasAI must accept logs/audit access for the pilot; no cross-region backups without signed approval).
- Liability cap aligned to pilot fees; no unlimited commitments.

Operational approvals required before we commit publicly: Product sign-off on architecture + estimated cost (Aisha), SE sign-off on capacity/runbook (Karthik), Security sign-off if they require deeper audit access (I can loop in Security if you flag it).

If everyone is comfortable I can draft an MSA addendum template and a short customer-facing pilot commitment letter. We should avoid promising hard financial credits beyond a small pilot-specific cap.

Laura
Laura Bennett
VP Revenue Operations (Legal Liaison)
Redwood Inference

Subject: AtlasAI pilot — proposed pilot approach and ask for confirmation

Ben —

Thanks for the conversation earlier. Internal alignment is mostly complete; here's our proposed approach for the 90-day pilot (summary):
- Start date: target May 3 — 90-day window
- Topline commitment: 99.9% availability for the pilot route; P95 target 120ms. Pilot fee covers dedicated preview pool and operational support.
- Proposed approach: Hybrid start — Hosted elevated routing + prefix caching for first 30 days, with a planned Dedicated pool spin-up by day 31 if traffic and conversion look promising.
- Required from AtlasAI: signed pilot addendum (attached), expected sample traffic day (CSV), and model hash if they require pinning.

Attachments: atlasai_sla_request_v1.pdf, atlasai_mutual_action_plan.xlsx

Next steps: please confirm acceptance of the approach and attach the sample traffic day by Friday. Once we have that we will provide a capacity/runbook and a DocuSign link for the pilot addendum.

Best —
Jasmine
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
